technical_body.statement: A bandlimited signal with maximum frequency f_max is fully determined by samples taken at fs > 2 * f_max.
technical_body.corollary: For a complex-baseband (IQ) signal, the bandwidth captured is exactly fs (not fs/2 — negative and positive frequencies both fit).
technical_body.numpy_sketch: For a real signal, fs > 2 * f_max. For IQ, fs is the total captured bandwidth.

technical_body.statement: Any frequency component above fs/2 (for real sampling) or outside [-fs/2, fs/2] (for IQ) folds into the visible band at f_aliased = f - k*fs for the k that puts it in range.
technical_body.workaround: Use an anti-alias filter before the ADC, or take samples fast enough that everything of interest is inside the Nyquist band.

technical_body.statement: An RF signal at carrier fc downconverted by an LO at fc produces I (in-phase) and Q (quadrature) baseband streams. Together they carry BOTH positive and negative frequency content, so a symmetric spectrum is *asymmetric* in IQ.
technical_body.numpy_sketch: iq = I + 1j*Q; positive freqs in np.fft.fft(iq) are 'above' the LO, negative freqs are 'below'

technical_body.trade: larger N -> finer frequency resolution but coarser time resolution
technical_body.numpy_sketch: spec = np.fft.fftshift(np.fft.fft(iq * window)); bins are np.linspace(-fs/2, fs/2, N)

technical_body.trade: wider main-lobe (Hann/Hamming) vs deeper sidelobes (Blackman-Harris) vs box (no window - worst leakage)
technical_body.typical_choice: Hann for spectrograms; Blackman-Harris for weak-signal detection alongside a strong nearby carrier

technical_body.statement: Split signal into overlapping windowed segments; take FFT of each; average magnitude squared. Reduces variance vs a single FFT.
technical_body.numpy_sketch: from scipy.signal import welch; f, Pxx = welch(iq, fs=fs, nperseg=4096, return_onesided=False)

technical_body.statement: For a real signal x(t), analytic(t) = x(t) + j * H{x}(t), where H{} removes the negative frequencies. Envelope = |analytic|.
technical_body.numpy_sketch: from scipy.signal import hilbert; envelope = np.abs(hilbert(x))

technical_body.statement: The linear filter maximizing SNR at the sampling instant is h(t) = p(-t) (time-reversed pulse shape). For symmetric pulses p, h(t) = p(t).
Lowpass filter, then take every K-th sample. Effective sample rate = fs/K.
technical_body.numpy_sketch: from scipy.signal import decimate; y = decimate(x, K, ftype='fir')

technical_body.statement: Change sample rate by rational factor P/Q using a single unified filter that both interpolates and decimates.
technical_body.numpy_sketch: from scipy.signal import resample_poly; y = resample_poly(x, up=P, down=Q)

technical_body.statement: Many modulations have a periodic autocorrelation structure — the spectral correlation function reveals the symbol rate as a distinct peak. Used for modulation classification.
technical_body.note: Second-pass depth; first pass just recognize the concept.

technical_body.cause: The LO leaks through the mixer to the ADC; sits at whatever frequency the tuner is set to (DC in complex baseband).
technical_body.workaround: Tune the LO off the signal of interest (offset by ~fs/4) then digitally shift back. See ai/prompts.py:110 for target_freq_hz vs center_freq_hz.

technical_body.cause: Non-ideal quadrature: the LO's I and Q outputs are not perfectly 90 deg apart or not perfectly equal in amplitude.
technical_body.visible_pathology: A mirror-image spectrum at -f (image rejection is finite).

technical_body.statement: For an amplitude-modulated (AM, OOK, ASK) signal, |iq| tracks the amplitude envelope.
For an FM / FSK signal, the derivative of unwrapped phase, scaled by fs/(2*pi), gives the instantaneous frequency in Hz.
PLL that locks to a suppressed carrier by mixing the input with I and Q locally generated tones; the loop filter drives the NCO. M-ary variants use M-power nonlinearity.
For an OOK/PSK stream with pulse duration T, autocorrelation of the envelope peaks at multiples of T. FFT of the autocorrelation reveals the symbol rate.
technical_body.numpy_sketch: ac = np.correlate(env, env, mode='full'); peaks = np.argmax(ac[len(ac)//2 + 1:]) + 1  # samples per symbol

technical_body.rule_of_thumb: SNR (dB) ~ 6.02 * bits + 1.76 for a full-scale sine
technical_body.notes: 8-bit ADC is why HackRF struggles with very-strong-nearby-weak-target scenarios.

technical_body.statement: A tone that lands between FFT bins is attenuated by the window's response at that fractional offset. Max scalloping loss for a rectangular window is ~3.9 dB; for Hann ~1.4 dB.
technical_body.workaround: Zero-pad the FFT (finer bin spacing) or fit a peak model to the three nearest bins.

technical_body.statement: Any signal at +f_offset appears as a weaker mirror at -f_offset due to IQ imbalance. HackRF image rejection is typically 30-40 dB unless corrected.
technical_body.correction: Estimate and null the mirror via signal-processing correction of I/Q gain + phase.

technical_body.statement: FM broadcast transmits with pre-emphasis boosting high audio frequencies; receiver applies matching de-emphasis (single-pole LPF, tau=75us US / 50us EU) to restore flat audio and improve SNR.

hackrf_stages: LNA at IF (0-40 dB, 8 dB steps)
technical_body.guideline: put LNA gain first to establish noise figure; add baseband VGA only up to just below ADC clipping

technical_body.statement: Sampling at k * Nyquist and then decimating spreads quantization noise over a wider band; low-pass and decimating retains signal SNR while shedding out-of-band noise. Effective bits ~ log2(k)/2 higher.
technical_body.numpy_sketch: capture at 20 Msps -> LPF -> decimate to 2 Msps for a 1.5-bit effective-ENOB improvement
